```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has a clearer B2B payer and a sourced price band. Support managers already buy per-agent seats at roughly $15–45/mo (Blitzz pricing) and $29–99/mo (CrankWheel pricing), and both are linked. B's payer is described loosely as 'operators, strategists, consultants' who may be 'self-funding,' which is a weaker buyer for a 90-day first sale.",
    "A has a named distribution channel with budget-primed buyers. The Zendesk Marketplace has no listing fee, and its buyers expect to spend $500–$5,000+/yr on add-ons (Vendr source). B's own brief concedes that its paid channels (~$104 CPL on Google, $8–12 CPC on LinkedIn) squeeze unit economics against a ~$60 one-off price, and that its organic channels are 'unquantified.'",
    "A has a plausible narrow wedge that avoids the heaviest gating. Small 5–20 agent support teams outside regulated verticals may not require SOC 2 or HIPAA, so a first paying customer within 90 days is conceivable. B's brief identifies no wedge at all against five near-identical competitors, and leaves 'what is the differentiated wedge' as an open question.",
    "B's brief admits a core trust problem in its category: vendors say humans must verify every number. It also raises an unanswered substitute threat from general-purpose LLM chat. Both undercut willingness to pay for a dedicated tool.",
    "A's risks are serious but bounded and named. Free substitutes (Quick Assist, JoinByKey) exist, and the demand quotes come from family caregivers rather than support-team payers. B's risks (saturation, a trust deficit, the LLM substitute, an episodic usage model) attack the premise of paying at all."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is the weakest item. Its two quotes describe general decision paralysis, not a need for an AI research tool or a willingness to pay. The LinkedIn quote ('the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.') actually argues against a tool producing the decision. A secondary weakness: the claim that competitors 'validate willingness to pay' rests on listed prices only. One competitor (Insightloop) is pre-launch, PREONZ pricing is NOT FOUND, and the 'funded-looking' description carries no source.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs are thin on payer-side demand. A's demand quotes come from consumers helping parents rather than support managers. A's '41% faster resolution, 47% higher FCR' figures have no source in the brief and were treated as missing. Its 'small teams are underserved' thesis is asserted rather than evidenced. A wins mainly because B's own brief documents more fundamental problems (unit economics, saturation, a trust gap, the LLM substitute) and offers no wedge."
}
```
